This tl.trans() forces Triton to stage the transposed tile through shared memory with a stride that causes 11.9-way bank conflicts. All prior attempts to fix this via tile-size changes while keeping tl.trans() produced correctness failures (max_diff ~70), indicating the block_ptr + tl.trans() combination has a layout/indexing bug for this kernel's stride configuration (stride_bn=240, stride_bk=1). The correct fix is to abandon tl.make_block_ptr for B and use classic pointer arithmetic to load B directly in (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N) layout — matching tl.dot's expected second operand without any transpose, eliminating shared memory staging and the bank conflicts.

Despite halving dynamic shared memory per block (32.77 KB → 16.38 KB), elapsed cycles increased from 47,229 to 57,481 and warp cycles per issued instruction worsened from 4.42 to 5.17. The bank conflict count remained essentially unchanged (~11.9-way, ~77.5% of wavefronts), indicating that num_stages/num_warps tuning alone cannot resolve bank conflicts that are inherent to the tile shape and access pattern. The regression likely stems from the autotuner selecting a suboptimal config (e.g., num_warps=8 with the same register-heavy kernel causing spilling or scheduling overhead) while the root bank-conflict bottleneck persists.

do_not_apply_when: When the primary bottleneck is SharedMemoryConflicts (11.9-way bank conflicts, >75% of shared load wavefronts conflicted).
